diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists an $r_{\lambda} < 0$ and a $C_2 > 0$ such that $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^\infty$ satisfies

issues.failure_explanation: Clause (v) imposes lambda_k <= C_2 k^{r_lambda} with r_lambda < 0, so the bound tends to 0, while the clause 'indexed so that they are non-decreasing in k' forces lambda_k >= lambda_1 for all k. For a covariance operator with lambda_1 > 0 this is contradictory, so (i)-(v) as written admit only the trivial zero-covariance case. The paper's principal example Q = sigma r^{-gamma}(kappa^2 - Delta)^{-beta} has strictly decreasing eigenvalues lambda_k = sigma r^{-gamma}(kappa^2+xi_k)^{-beta} (the joint indexing is fixed by (iii) and by mu_k non-decreasing in (iv)), so it does not satisfy the clause either. The clause is a slip for 'non-increasing'; no proof in the paper uses any monotonicity of lambda_k, only the bound lambda_k <= C_2 k^{r_lambda}.

failure_location.quote: where the eigenvalues $\{\lambda_k\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ are indexed so that they are non-decreasing in $k$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'non-decreasing' by 'non-increasing' (or delete the indexing clause) in Assumption (v); since no argument uses the clause, nothing else changes.
issues.overall_effect: Read literally, the hypotheses of thm:spectral-convergence, cor:laplacian-spectral-convergence and thm:main-result (all of which assume assumption:operator) are met by no nontrivial model, including the operators in (eq:operators) that the paper is about, so the stated theory has no genuine instances as written.
issues.title: Assumption (v) requires the lambda_k to be non-decreasing yet satisfy a decaying bound, which no nontrivial Q can satisfy
issues.why_classification: A one-word, forced repair; the clause is never used in any proof, so every result, rate, and the advertised scope survive verbatim.

issues.failure_explanation: Var(omega_k(t)) = t <Q e_k, e_k>/lambda_k. Under (i)-(ii) the e_k are eigenfunctions of A only, so <Q e_k, e_k> need not equal lambda_k: e.g. with lambda_1 = 1, lambda_2 = 2 and e_1 = (f_1+f_2)/sqrt(2) (an eigenbasis of some A), Var(omega_1(t)) = 3t/2, so omega_1 is a Wiener process but not a standard one. Standardness holds exactly when e_k is also Q's eigenfunction, i.e. under (iii), which the lemma invokes only for the independence claim. The proof's justification 'By definition ... are standard Wiener-processes' is therefore invalid under the stated hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore the processes $\{\omega_k(t)\}_{k = 1}^{\infty}$ are $\mathbb{R}$-valued, standard Wiener-processes.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add assumption:operator(iii) to the hypotheses for the 'Furthermore' claim (or weaken it to: omega_k is a Wiener process with variance t<Qe_k,e_k>/lambda_k).
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's auxiliary claim is false as stated; the representation formula itself is unaffected. All downstream uses (the Itô isometry in the proof of thm:spectral-convergence, the set-up of thm-convergence) assume the full assumption:operator including (iii), so they remain valid once the hypothesis is added.
issues.title: omega_k are declared standard Wiener processes under assumptions (i)-(ii) only
issues.why_classification: Adding an already-available, standard hypothesis repairs the claim with no change to any downstream result, method, or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: From xi_k >= C_Delta k^{2/d} one obtains mu_k = r^{-1}(kappa^2+xi_k)^alpha >= r^{-1} C_Delta^alpha k^{2 alpha/d} and lambda_k = sigma r^{-gamma}(kappa^2+xi_k)^{-beta} <= sigma r^{-gamma} C_Delta^{-beta} k^{-2 beta/d}. The proof instead asserts these bounds with C_Delta in place of C_Delta^alpha and C_Delta^{-beta}; for example when C_Delta < 1 the claimed upper bound on lambda_k is smaller than the valid one and may fail. Thus C_1 = r^{-1}C_Delta and C_2 = sigma r^{-gamma}C_Delta are not legitimate choices in general, and the constant stated in the corollary (proportional to C_Delta^{2-2gamma}) is not the one the argument yields; the correct computation gives C_Delta^{-(beta+(2gamma-1)alpha)}, so the printed bound can be false, although the rate M^{-2 nu/d} is correct.

failure_location.quote: satisfy the bounds $r^{-1} C_\Delta k^{\frac{2 \alpha}{d}}\leq \mu_k$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma} C_\Delta k^{- \frac{2 \beta}{d}}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use C_1 = r^{-1} C_Delta^alpha and C_2 = sigma r^{-gamma} C_Delta^{-beta}, and restate the constant as C = sigma r^{gamma-1} C_Delta^{-(beta+(2gamma-1)alpha)} Gamma(2gamma-1)/Gamma(gamma)^2 * d/(2 nu).
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant in cor:laplacian-spectral-convergence is unreliable; the convergence rate, which is the only content used downstream (e.g. 'the spectral part of the error converges like M^{1 - (2/d)(beta + (2 gamma - 1) alpha)}' and the predicted numerical order nu_s/2), is unaffected.
issues.title: Wrong explicit constant in cor:laplacian-spectral-convergence: exponents of C_Delta dropped in C_1 and C_2
issues.why_classification: A local, mechanical recomputation of the constant; the rate and every substantive claim survive and no dependent result uses the constant.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof ends with a bound on the root-mean-square error whose prefactor is sqrt(lambda_k)/Gamma(gamma) (Part 2 similarly yields sqrt(lambda_k) mu_k^{-1/q}, and Part 4 a single factor (1+sqrt(log))). Squaring, as the stated left-hand side E|c_k - c̃_k|^2 requires, gives lambda_k (respectively mu_k^{-2/q}, delta_{gamma,h}^2), not sqrt(lambda_k) (respectively mu_k^{-1/q}, delta_{gamma,h}). Since c_k is proportional to sqrt(lambda_k), the true error is exactly linear in lambda_k, so with a constant depending only on C_Pi, t, gamma the stated sqrt(lambda_k)-bound fails for large lambda_k (e.g. gamma = 2, m = 0: the error is Theta(lambda_k h^2)). The squared factors are also exactly what thm:main-result uses (C''_M = C sum_{k<=M} lambda_k and mu_k^{-2/q}), confirming the statement is the unsquared version of what is proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace sqrt(lambda_k) by lambda_k, mu_k^{-1/q} by mu_k^{-2/q}, and delta_{gamma,h} by delta_{gamma,h}^2 in thm-convergence and in the two corollaries, matching the proofs and thm:main-result.
issues.overall_effect: The temporal error bounds stated in thm-convergence and repeated in cor:projection-method and cor:order-0-method assert a sqrt(lambda_k)-dependence (with mu_k^{-1/q} and a single delta_{gamma,h}) that the proofs do not establish and that is false as a lambda_k-uniform statement; the convergence rates in h are correct. thm:main-result is already stated with the corrected lambda_k-structure.
issues.title: thm-convergence states the mean-square bound with the unsquared root-mean-square constants (sqrt(lambda_k) instead of lambda_k)
issues.why_classification: The correction is forced by the paper's own proof and by thm:main-result; all convergence rates, regimes, and guarantees are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that $\Pi_m$ is such that $\Pi_m g = g$ for all $g \in \mathcal{P}_m(\mathcal{I})$ and that $\Pi_m$ satisfies $\norm{\Pi_m h}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t))} \leq C_\Pi \norm{h}_{\mathcal{L}^2([0,t))}$ for some $C_\Pi > 0$

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed estimate tacitly replaces ||Pi_m g - Pi_m f_t|| by ||Pi_m(g - f_t)|| before applying the assumed boundedness; that step uses additivity of Pi_m, which is not among the hypotheses (only Pi_m g = g on P_m(I) and boundedness on the affine family g + alpha f_t are assumed). Linearity is essential, not cosmetic: the nonlinear map Pi_m h := pi_m h + w * 1{h = f_t}, with w in P_m(I), ||w|| = 1, satisfies both stated hypotheses with a mesh-independent C_Pi (the indicator fires only at h = f_t since f_t is not piecewise polynomial), but ||f_t - Pi_m f_t||_{L^2} -> 1 as h -> 0, so E|c_k - c̃_k^{(m)}|^2 = Theta(lambda_k) does not converge, refuting the theorem's conclusion. The same insufficient hypothesis is repeated in thm:main-result. Both examples used in the paper (the L^2-projection pi_m and the point-evaluation map Pi_0) are linear.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that Pi_m is linear; both pi_m and Pi_0 comply, so no other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, thm-convergence and thm:main-result are false: their hypotheses admit nonlinear maps Pi_m for which the temporal (and hence the full) discretisation error does not converge at all.
issues.title: Missing linearity hypothesis on Pi_m in thm-convergence
issues.why_classification: A one-word additional hypothesis that all intended examples satisfy; every conclusion, rate, and downstream result is preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: & \leq C_{\Pi}^2 \sum_{\ell = 1}^n \left[ g_\ell^2 (t_\ell - t_{\ell - 1}) + 2 \alpha g_\ell \int_{t_{\ell - 1}}^{t_\ell} f_{t_n}(s) \, \text{d}s + \alpha^2 \int_{t_{\ell - 1}}^{t_\ell} f_{t_n}(s)^2 \, \text{d}s  \right] \\

issues.failure_explanation: The cross term 2 alpha g_l (t_n - s̃_l)^{gamma-1} h_l is bounded term-by-term via the positive-quantity comparability (t_n - s̃_l)^{gamma-1} h_l \lesssim gamma ∫ f_{t_n} coming from lem:boundedness-p0-inequalities. But alpha and g_l are arbitrary reals: multiplying the comparability by 2 alpha g_l < 0 reverses the inequality, so the displayed step, and hence the final assembly of ||Pi_0(g + alpha f)||^2 <= C_Pi^2 ||g + alpha f||^2, is invalid exactly on the cells where the cross term is negative. What the conclusion actually requires is a uniform (in g_l, alpha, and the mesh, with constant depending only on theta, gamma, k̄) comparison of the quadratic forms h_l (g_l + alpha a_l)^2 and ∫_{I_l} (g_l + alpha f_{t_n})^2 per cell — equivalently (a_l - f̄_l)^2 \lesssim Var_l(f_{t_n}) — and no such argument appears in the proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the cross-term estimate by a per-cell uniform equivalence of quadratic forms: from lem:boundedness-p0-inequalities one gets a_l \asymp f̄_l and overline{f^2}_l \asymp f̄_l^2 (the last cell treated separately), hence (a_l - f̄_l)^2 <= C Var_l and (g + alpha a_l)^2 <= C'(g^2 + 2 alpha g f̄_l + alpha^2 overline{f^2}_l) with constants depending only on theta, gamma, k̄; summation over l then yields the lemma.
issues.overall_effect: lem:boundedness-p0 is unproved as written; its boundedness constant C_Pi feeds cor:order-0-method, and through it the temporal and full error bounds for the piecewise-constant theta-scheme X̃^{h,0}_M that is tested numerically. The lemma's statement is correct and the missing estimate does hold, so the damage is to the proof, not to the claim.
issues.title: Proof of lem:boundedness-p0 estimates signed cross terms as if they were positive, so the termwise comparison is invalid
issues.why_classification: The central estimate of the proof must be replaced by a contained but nontrivial argument (a uniform 2x2 quadratic-form comparison); the lemma statement and all downstream rates survive, so no global restructuring or loss of content occurs.

issues.failure_explanation: The forward relations give (2 gamma - 1) alpha = beta_s (nu_s + d/2); solving with the printed gamma in both regimes (beta_s below or above beta*) yields alpha = (nu_s/(2 nu_t)) min(1, beta_s/beta*), so the printed formula for alpha is exactly twice the correct inverse. Concretely, for the sphere simulation's targets nu_s = nu_t = 1, beta_s = 0.5, d = 2 the printed formula gives alpha = 1, which inserted into the forward map yields nu_s = 2 and beta_s = 2/3, not the requested values; the paper's own simulations use alpha = 0.5, consistent with the corrected formula. The displayed claim that this is an equivalent parametrisation is therefore false as printed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace alpha = (nu_s/nu_t) min(1, beta_s/beta*) by alpha = (nu_s/(2 nu_t)) min(1, beta_s/beta*).
issues.overall_effect: A reader using the printed reparametrisation (stated to be used 'throughout the numerical experiment') obtains a doubled alpha and hence fields with different spatial/temporal smoothness than intended; the paper's numerical results themselves were produced with the correct mapping and are unaffected.
issues.title: Inverse reparametrisation formula for alpha is off by a factor of 2
issues.why_classification: A single forced correction, confirmed by internal consistency (the forward formulas and the paper's own parameter values); no theorem or numerical result depends on the misprint.
